title: Adaptive Dashboards & Cost Decomposition — launch orchestration, training & sales enablement
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Coordinate a cross-functional launch for the Adaptive Dashboards feature set: adaptive dashboard layouts, cost decomposition cards, and rollout controls. This ticket owns orchestration across Product, Engineering, Design, Docs, Sales Enablement, and Customer Success to ensure the feature ships with coherent release notes, localized training assets, and a staged rollout plan with canary cohorts. Scope includes: finalizing release copy, creating in-product tooltips, recording two short demo videos (PM overview + sales pitch), an internal enablement webinar, and a pilot program with three strategic customers. We need to align on gating criteria, fallback behavior, and analytics instrumentation for post-launch quality monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: Release notes draft completed and reviewed by Docs, Marketing, and Legal
Two demo videos produced and uploaded to Drive (PM overview, Sales pitch)
Sales enablement playbook and 30-minute training session scheduled and slotted into Sales weekly cadence
In-product 'What's New' tooltip and links to help center implemented and QA'd
Pilot cohort of 3 customers onboarded and feedback loop defined
Canary rollout flag implemented with automated rollback policy and metrics tracked in Console (error rate, latency, adoption)
Localization: release notes + tooltips translated to EN, FR, DE, JP for targeted regions

release_notes_blurb: Adaptive Dashboards: Dynamic layout and cost decomposition cards that surface per-route and per-model token cost. Rollouts will be controlled via feature flags with canary cohorts. Learn more in the in-product tour and Help Center.
rollout_plan_summary: Wave 0 (Internal + Pilot): enable for selected pilot customers and internal accounts (1 week). Wave 1 (Canary): 5% of eligible orgs via feature flag, monitor adoption and errors (1 week). Wave 2 (Gradual): 25% then 100% over two weeks contingent on SLOs. Automated rollback on error rate > 1% or latency regression > 20% vs baseline.
